Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Salt Lake City UT
513 AM MST Mon Nov 2 2026

.KEY MESSAGES, Issued 1037 PM MST Sun Nov 1 2026...


- Accumulating mountain snow is expected across all Utah mountains 
through  Monday morning. Upwards of 12" of snow is expected above 
9000   feet, and 3-6" of snow down to around 7000 feet. Upper 
elevations of the Cottonwoods and western Uintas may see   localized 
accumulations 18-24".  

- Cool, dry, and stable conditions build in Tuesday following the 
passage of this system. 

- A weak system looks to impact the region Wednesday/Thursday 
ushering in a brief period of low elevation rainfall and high 
elevation snowfall across primarily northern and central Utah. 

&&

.DISCUSSION, Issued 1037 PM MST Sun Nov 1 2026...
Currently, a mid-level trough is traversing across the 
Great Basin with its axis nearly centered along the UT/NV border. 
With this trough, a cold front continues to sweep across much of UT, 
having already traversed the western half of the state. While the 
lower levels are slowly drying out, weak ascent with modest moisture 
aloft will result in light to occasionally moderate rainfall 
persisting across much of the forecast area through roughly 09z. 
From 09z on, higher terrain will be favored for precipitation given 
drier low levels of the atmosphere. As such, the flood watch will be 
allowed to expire at 06z for southern UT and portions of central UT. 

700mb temperatures will continue to cool following the passage of 
the cold front to roughly -3C to -4C resulting in snow levels 
continuing to drop through the evening to around 6500ft. 
Additionally, northwest flow aloft will persist, resulting in a 
favorable pattern for widespread mountain snow across much of Utah's 
high terrain. Of note, a TROWAL feature has been identified via 
satellite imagery serving to wrap more moisture around the northwest 
side of a deepening upper low located over northern UT. This has 
resulted in another round of widespread light to moderate rain 
observed across northern UT, and will also contribute to snowfall 
totals across our northern UT mountains. Across our UT high terrain 
(generally 9000ft or greater), 3-6" of additional snowfall is 
expected. Some areas, such as the Upper Cottonwoods and Western 
Uintas may see additional snowfall totals from 6-12" given favorable 
northwest flow orientation overnight. 

Transient ridging builds in Monday in the wake of the deepening 
trough as it progresses east. This will result in most precipitation 
coming to a halt across the forecast area, though some lingering 
showers across the UT high terrain may persist. This feature is 
forecast to persist through Tuesday bringing quiescent conditions 
and unseasonably cool temperatures, potentially as low a 15F below 
seasonal normals areawide. 

Ensemble guidance has come into better agreement with a weak mid-
level trough sweeping through the Great Basin on Wednesday. This 
system is not expected to bring a whole lot of moisture with it, and 
with weak forcing, only light valley rainfall with light mountain 
snow accumulations are expected across northern and central UT. 
Following this system, dry conditions develop once again as ridging 
becomes dominant across much of the western U.S. through the 
remainder of the week and into the weekend. 


&&

.AVIATION...
KSLC...As showers wind down this morning, expect to see improving 
conditions, with prevailing VFR returning by 13z. However, CIGS may 
remain below 7kft through 15-16z with mountain top obscurations. 
Northerly winds will prevail before a shift to southerly drainage 
winds occur around 02-03z. 

REST OF UTAH AND SOUTHWEST WYOMING...As showers wind down this 
morning, expect to see improving conditions across the airspace, with 
prevailing VFR returning after 13-15z at most sites. However, low 
CIGS may continue to result in mountain top obscurations through at 
least 16z. Some low-lying valleys may see fog develop tonight, with 
greatest potential at KLGU. West to northwest winds will be in place 
across most terminals today behind a cold front, with a return to 
diurnal drainage winds this evening.

&&
